question.leadin: At the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander the Great defeated forces from this empire.
question.text: Name this empire, which was ruled for some periods by Achaemenids, Safavids, and Afshars. Rulers of this empire included Cyrus the Great and Xerxes (ZERK-seez) the Great.
question.clue: A ruler of this empire was assassinated by Artabanus, the commander of this empire's royal bodyguard, the Immortals.

swap.leadin: Give the following related to first Persian invasion of Greece.
swap.text: This "Great" Persian leader, who avenged the death of Cyrus the Great by attacking Scythia, invaded Greece after the Ionian Revolt.
swap.clue: This leader of an expedition against the Scythians divided his empire into twenty satrapies, and he built a noted network of roads.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force.
question.text: SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country's city of Tehran.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]
question.clue: This country created a literacy corps as part of its White Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about civilizations that relied on horse archers.
swap.text: Retreating horse archers would turn around to shoot arrows at the enemy in a "shot" named for this empire. This Persian empire between that of the Seleucids and the Sassanids used horse archers in their defeat of Crassus at the Battle of Carrhae.
swap.answerHtml: Parthian Empire [accept Arsacid dynasty or empire; accept Parthian shot]
swap.clue: This empire's namesake "shot" consisted of turning around on horseback during retreat to fire at the advancing army.

question.leadin: This victor of the battles of Ipsus and Corupedium was succeeded in his highest post by his son Antiochus after his assassination.
question.text: Name this Diadochos who established a namesake empire in the former easternmost satrapies of Alexander the Great.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.leadin: Translations of the Hebrew Bible into this language were known as targum.
swap.text: Name this ancient Semitic language, used as a lingua franca in Mesopotamia and Judea. Jesus Christ spoke this language inscribed on the sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II.
swap.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the life of the Byzantine emperor Justinian in 532 A.D.
question.text: In September 532, Justinian signed an "Eternal Peace" with Khosrau I, a king of this empire. Another ruler of this empire captured the Roman emperor Valerian after the Battle of Edessa.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.text: This ruler of the Sassanid (SASS-uh-nid) dynasty signed the Perpetual Peace with Justinian. This ruler persecuted a sect called the Mazdakites (MAZ-dak-ites) for supporting his brother Kawus, who opposed his rule.

question.text: This Achaemenid public works project linked Susa, a capital in modern-day Iran, to Sardis in Anatolia. It allowed horse-mounted mail couriers to go super-fast.
question.clue: This was the name given to the ancient highway that connected Susa to Sardis in the Persian Empire. This was also the name given by the Spanish to the more notable parts of the Inca road system.

swap.text: This Persian king invaded Greece, beating the 300 at the battle of Thermopylae. His ships lost at Salamis.
swap.answer: Xerxes I or Xerxes the Great

question.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
question.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

swap.text: A university at Gondishapur that was established by this Persian dynasty contained an advanced hospital that gave accreditation to local physicians. This dynasty was founded by Ardashir and included rulers like Shapur.
swap.answerHtml: Sassanian dynasty [or Sassanid Empire; accept the House of Sasan]
swap.clue: This last pre-Islamic Persian dynasty, which unsuccessfully besieged Constantinople in 626.

question.leadin: A widely rejected theory links the language of this ancient kingdom to South India's Dravidian language family.
question.text: Name this kingdom in modern Western Iran whose king, Shutruk-Nahhunte, took the stelae ("STEE-lee") of the Babylonian kings Naram-Sin and Hammurabi back to his capital of Susa during a 12th-century BC invasion of the Kassite Dynasty.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.text: The first Parthian king of this name, who styled himself as "Philhellene", greatly expanded the empire by taking Mesopotamia. A king of Pontus with this name immunized himself from poison by taking small doses.
swap.clue: After conquering the territory of Nicomedes IV of Bithynia, a king of this name massacred all of its Roman citizens in the "Asiatic Vespers".

question.text: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.
question.clue: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.

swap.text: One of the earliest Buddhist missionaries to China, An Shigao, was supposedly a prince of this empire, which was known as "Anxi" ("an-shee") in China. The diplomat Gan Ying visited this empire on a fact-finding mission.
swap.clue: It was ruled by the Arsacid line and supplanted by Ardashir's Sassanids.

question.leadin: Its capital was known as Ecbatana to the Greeks, and was probably founded by Cyaxeres.
question.text: Name this empire, whose last ruler Astyages was overtrown by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.text: The Battle of al-Qadisayyah forced this last Sassanian emperor to flee; he was killed by a miller in 651, ending the Sassanian dynasty.

question.leadin: Little is known about this figure, but according to Plutarch, he was tall, and was very manly despite the "delicacy of his looks and effeminacy of his dress."
question.text: Name this Spahbod who was sent by Orodes II to delay the Romans, but ended up defeating them instead, using horse-archers and camels to resupply the archers.
question.clue: According to Plutarch's Parallel Lives, a commander fighting against this leader had to rescind an attempted charge when he saw that his soldier's "hands were riveted to their shields and their feet nailed through and through to the ground" by arrows.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a delightful tale of deception, cannibalism, and betrayal.
swap.text: This general had to eat his own son after Astyages discovered he did not actually murder an infant prophesied to overthrow him. He would later understandably mutiny against Astyages at the Battle of Pasargadae.
swap.clue: Upon arriving in Susa, Alexander found that this treasurer had taken large quantities of money and soldiers and bolted town for Athens. This man was eventually killed in Crete.
